import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths as given
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_39/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_39/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_39/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_39/test_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_39/test_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_39/test_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_39/test_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_39/test_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_39/test_8.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_39/test_9.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_39/test_10.csv"
]

# Since all source tables have the exact same schema ['0'] and the target schema is also ['0'],
# the transformation plan is to UNION ALL the data from all source tables into one DataFrame.
# According to Hint 2 and Hint 4, UNION is the correct operation here.

# Read all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)  # index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
    # Ensure the column '0' is integer type as per target schema
    df['0'] = df['0'].astype(int)
    dfs.append(df)

# Concatenate all DataFrames vertically (UNION ALL)
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# The target table name is Target9_39, but since we are writing to CSV, we just save the result.
# Write the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_39/target_multisource_cot.csv"
target_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
